insights.headline: Gold steadies near $4,180 after its longest weekly slide in a decade as gold ETF money rotates from the US to Asia
insights.summary: Spot gold held around $4,160–$4,187 on Tuesday after a sixth straight weekly decline — the longest in a decade — as the dollar index broke out to an 18-month high of 102.59. US-listed gold ETFs fell to a record-low 49.6% share of global holdings while Asia drove nearly half of the past year’s 402-tonne growth, per WGC data. On MCX, December gold futures chopped around ₹1,49,500–1,49,900 per 10 grams and silver near ₹2.23 lakh per kg, with the rupee in the mid-90s after RBI FX curbs. Festive demand builds ahead of Dhanteras and Diwali; Kanpur police are probing a fake-hallmarking racket.
points: US gold ETF share of global holdings hit a record-low 49.6%; Asia drove 48.5% of 402t growth to September (WGC).
Dollar index at 102.59, highest since April 2025; December Fed hike odds near 85%, per one analyst.
MCX gold Dec futures ~₹1,49,500–1,49,900/10g; silver ~₹2.22–2.24 lakh/kg; rupee in mid-90s on RBI curbs.
Kanpur police probe 25–30 machines suspected of printing fake BIS hallmarks ahead of Dhanteras/Diwali.
Kazakhstan to trim gold to 75% of reserves; China keeps buying despite the price slump.

trending.title: ETF money rotates east as gold slides
trending.summary: US-listed gold ETFs fell to a record-low 49.6% of global holdings while Asia drove nearly half of the past year’s 402-tonne growth — the bid has moved east even as prices fell six straight weeks.

trending.title: Dollar breakout pins gold; hike bets linger
trending.summary: The dollar index hit an 18-month high of 102.59 and December hike odds sit near 85%, keeping gold’s rebound capped below $4,251. One read: gold’s reaction is delayed, not cancelled.

trending.title: MCX gold hugs ₹1.50 lakh; firm rupee helps
trending.summary: December gold futures chopped around ₹1,49,500–1,49,900 per 10g with silver near ₹2.23 lakh/kg; the rupee’s rebound to the mid-90s on RBI FX curbs is cushioning import costs.

trending.title: Festive demand builds — verify before you buy
trending.summary: With Dhanteras and Diwali approaching, hopes are pinned on festive buying; Kanpur’s fake-hallmarking probe is a reminder to verify HUID details on the BIS Care app before purchasing.

trending.title: Central banks split: Kazakhstan trims, China adds
trending.summary: Kazakhstan plans to cut gold from 78% to 75% of reserves by year-end as Treasury yields burnish the dollar’s appeal, while China keeps buying through the slump.

items.title: US Gold ETFs Hit Record-Low Market Share as Asia Expands on Falling Price
items.summary: Gold fell on Tuesday as US bond markets reopened, extending its losing streak to six weeks — the longest in a decade. US-listed gold ETFs now hold a record-low 49.6% of global gold ETF assets (51.9% at the start of the year), per WGC data. Asia drove 48.5% of the 402-tonne growth in global gold ETF holdings over the year to September, while Comex speculative net longs shrank by almost a quarter.

items.title: Gold firms as dollar, yields and oil retreat before CPI
items.summary: Spot gold firmed to $4,186.90 an ounce, up 0.39%, with silver near steady at $60.21 in early US trading Tuesday, as a softer dollar, lower Treasury yields (10-year near 5.19%) and retreating oil supported metals ahead of Wednesday's US CPI. Whether the data confirms the post-payrolls Fed-pause trade or revives December hike bets is the key question; September payrolls rose by just 29,000.

items.title: Gold Ignores the Dollar’s New High: Strength or Delay?
items.summary: The dollar index broke out to 102.59, its highest since April 2025, yet gold held above its lows — a divergence the author reads as delayed rather than cancelled selling, citing September’s pattern that ended with gold’s worst one-day fall of 2026. Silver and miners are not confirming strength; record ETF inflows reflect headline hedging, the piece argues, not a new bull market.

items.title: Gold, silver prices trade lower on MCX as firm dollar weighs on bullion
items.summary: Gold and silver traded lower on the MCX as a firm dollar weighed on bullion. On Comex, silver opened at $60.55 an ounce and traded marginally lower at $60.48, with gold near $4,200 and silver near $60.50 globally. Domestic silver faced fresh technical selling even as global prices held steadier through the session.

items.title: Gold Slips Below Rs 1.50 Lakh Mark On October 13
items.summary: MCX December gold fell over Rs 150 to Rs 1,49,535 per 10 grams in early trade -- below Rs 1.50 lakh for a second straight session -- while December silver slipped nearly Rs 500 to Rs 2,22,400 per kg. Both recovered after the first hour: by ~10:40 AM gold was Rs 1,49,876 (+0.22%) and silver Rs 2,23,113 (+0.11%). Retail 24K ranged Rs 1,48,340-1,49,620 per 10 grams across cities.

items.title: Rupee outpaces Asian peers on fresh FX curbs, RBI intervention
items.summary: The rupee outperformed Asian peers on Tuesday, touching 95.0725 before settling at 95.28, up 0.5% on the RBI's fresh FX curbs and likely spot-market intervention. The steps re-route oil importers' dollar demand to a special facility and cap no-exposure derivative trades at $5 million, down from $100 million. Analysts said markets increasingly see 97.00 per dollar as a level the RBI will defend.

items.title: RBI to continue efforts to curb rupee volatility; external factors driving currency fall: FM
items.summary: At the Bloomberg New Economy Forum 2026, FM Nirmala Sitharaman said the RBI will keep acting to curb excessive rupee volatility, stressing it is not 'fixing' the rupee. The 18-month fall stems mainly from external challenges, she said. The RBI's weekend package -- a special dollar window for oil companies and tighter forex-derivative rules -- lifted the rupee about 1% on Monday.

items.title: Silver Price Forecast – Silver Continues to Sit on Demand Zone
items.summary: Silver futures hovered near $60.67, sitting atop a $55-$60 demand zone that buyers are defending, with moving averages at $63.62 and $65.11. Softer US yields gave slight relief early Tuesday, but energy-inflation worries keep trade noisy -- "silver will be noisy until we get energy under control." Wednesday's US CPI is the next trigger for the non-yielding metal.

items.title: Kazakhstan's central bank plans to reduce gold share in reserves to 75%
items.summary: The National Bank of Kazakhstan plans to cut gold's share of its reserves from about 78% to 75% by year-end as surging US Treasury yields favour dollar assets, Bloomberg reported. Half the cut will come from selling options, half from physical sales. Kazakhstan was the world's fourth-largest gold buyer in January-August 2026, while China and Poland led buying; gold held near $4,172 an ounce.

items.title: China steps up gold buying despite slump in prices
items.summary: China's central bank added 740,000 troy ounces of gold in September, a 23rd straight month of net buying, taking holdings to about 2,387 tonnes; the country spent $158.8 billion on gold in January–August. Spot gold rose 0.4% to $4,185.69 on Tuesday as the dollar softened. Analysts say Chinese buying cushions the downside, but a strong dollar and hawkish Fed outlook remain the key risks.

items.title: Russia Pounds Ukrainian Energy Despite Trump's Ceasefire Announcement -- Commodities Roundup
items.summary: Russian strikes hit Ukrainian energy infrastructure hours after President Trump declared an "energy ceasefire", Dow Jones reports. Gold futures fell 0.6% to $4,191.80 a troy ounce while Brent crude rose 2.2% to $106.94. Trump also moved to allow Russian diesel exports to the US, saying Moscow would release 4.8 million tons -- though Jefferies doubts it will cool prices much.

items.title: Kanpur Police Probe Fake Gold Hallmarking Racket Involving 25–30 Machines
items.summary: Kanpur police are probing a fake-hallmarking racket ahead of Dhanteras and Diwali: 25–30 laser engraving machines allegedly misused to print counterfeit BIS hallmarks on jewellery. The probe began after a woman was caught selling a chain with an 18-carat hallmark holding only about 10% gold. BIS now shows jewellery photographs alongside HUID numbers in its BIS Care app for verification.

items.title: Gold cheaper by ₹1,750 in two days to ₹1.48 lakh/10g; experts see ₹1.55 lakh by Diwali
items.summary: IBJA data shows 10 grams of 24K gold fell Rs 399 to about Rs 1.48 lakh on October 13 -- roughly Rs 1,750 cheaper over two days -- while 1 kg of silver fell Rs 923 to about Rs 2.20 lakh. Commodity expert Ajay Kedia expects festival-season demand in India and China plus continued central-bank buying to lift gold toward Rs 1.55 lakh and silver toward Rs 2.40 lakh by Diwali.

items.title: Gold jewellery gets costlier as prices surge 54%; shoppers turn to Rs 10,000-Rs 1 lakh diamond pieces
items.summary: Gold is up about 54% since last year’s festive season, and Indian shoppers are shifting toward diamond-studded pieces in the Rs 10,000–Rs 1 lakh range, with retailers expecting 15–20% diamond sales growth. Jewellers are using 18-, 14- and 9-carat gold and lighter designs to keep pieces affordable — the festive-season trade-off between high prices and budget-conscious buying.

items.title: Gold, Silver Prices: Should You Buy During This Festive Season? Expert Shares Outlook
items.summary: With gold near ₹1.5 lakh/10g and silver above ₹2 lakh/kg heading into Navratri and Dhanteras, ETV Bharat quotes Kedia Advisory's Ajay Suresh Kedia, who puts gold support near ₹1,45,000–1,46,000 and silver near ₹2,10,000, with year-end upside scenarios of ₹1,75,000–1,80,000 for gold and ₹2,90,000–3,00,000 for silver. Spot gold eased toward $4,150/oz as the dollar touched an 18-month high.

items.title: Festive Buying Meets Global Pullback: How To Read Gold's 23% Correction From Record Highs Ahead Of Dhanteras
items.summary: With Dhanteras on November 6, Outlook Money breaks down gold's ~23% slide from its record to ~$4,185 on October 12. MCX December-4 futures traded at Rs 1,50,001/10g, 16% below their Rs 1,77,590 peak. Surging US Treasury yields drove the correction, the piece notes, citing Mirae Asset's 'Why Gold ETF Now?' thesis — leaving festive buyers weighing whether the pullback is a buying window.
